title: Example 17-12: Crossed-Out Letters and Insertions

illustrates.quote: Text may show crossed-out letters, words, or passages, along with substitutions in enclosure symbols. a. Follow the guidelines in Formats, §17.11 for transcribing crossed-out letters. b. Follow print for use and spacing of enclosure symbols.

blocks.text: Words with crossed-out letters are uncontracted, then repeated with a hyphen substituted for each crossed-out letter.

print.notes: Two sentences, each with a crossed-out-letter word immediately followed by a bracketed insertion.

braille.notes: A had the correct margin (10-space) and content; B had a spurious extra leading space (11 instead of 10) on the three TN lines only. Re-derived directly from source (margin 10 throughout): matches A exactly.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille: A's version kept (B had a 1-cell-too-deep TN margin on its first 3 lines). illustrates.rule unchanged ('17.12.2', both agreed, matches source). Modeled the same way as Example 17-9 (standalone TN + sentences with the repeated word in ordinary parentheses) — same F-211 inline-TN gap expected.
